title: Unit normalization of the actual-ring open pullback square
statement: Let $p:P\to T$ and $j:U\to T$ be morphisms of schemes, with $j$ an open immersion [def-pc-scheme; def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the canonical fibre product $P_U=P\times_TU$, its projections $a:P_U\to P$, $b:P_U\to U$, and its canonical chosen Cartesian-square record [def-pc-fibre-product; def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. For a commutative ring sheaf $R$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $R_P=p^{-1}R$, $R_U=j^{-1}R$ and $R_{P_U}=a^{-1}R_P$, and use the canonical $\operatorname{coefficientIso}:b^{-1}R_U\simeq R_{P_U}$ [def-sf-proetale-open-restriction-data]. Let $r=\operatorname{actualSquare}(p,j,R)$ be the strict ringed square with identity coefficient comparisons on the other three edges [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations]. Let $\alpha:r.\operatorname{exchangeModuleSquare}^{-1}:a^{-1}p^{-1}\simeq b^{-1}j^{-1}$ be its inverse module pullback comparison. Then $\alpha$ satisfies $\operatorname{AlphaNormalization}(p,j,R,\alpha)$: for every $R$-module sheaf $N$, site object $V\to T$ and section $m\in N(V)$, applying $\alpha_N$ to the iterated adjunction-unit section $\eta_{a,p^{-1}N}(\eta_{p,N}(m))$ equals restricting the iterated section $\eta_{b,j^{-1}N}(\eta_{j,N}(m))$ along the component at $V$ of the canonical site-square isomorphism $\operatorname{squareSiteIso}(p,j)$. The ordinary adjunctions, units and section restriction are those in the cited open-restriction data. This asserts only a unit equation for the inverse-image compositor; no sectionwise exchange comparison, derived category or resolution occurs.

proof.text: For each ordinary module compositor, apply unit_conjugateEquiv and evaluate on a module, site object and section. Its sectionwise conjugate is the canonical Over.pullbackComp restriction, by exchangeModuleComposition_existsUnique.choose_spec.1. This gives exchangeComposition_unit, identifying the compositor applied to the composite unit with the two iterated units after site restriction.

Regard a morphism and its coefficient comparison as a dependent pair. Equality induction proves that transport of the module pullback carries its unit to the transported unit, after restriction along the equality transport of site base change. For a commutative ringed square, exchangeCoefficients_eq supplies this equality. Paste the two compositor-unit identities with this transport: naturality moves the inverse compositor across the site restriction; invertibility of that restriction cancels it, and functoriality composes the site maps. The resulting map is the inverse first fibre-product compositor, the site equality transport, then the second fibre-product compositor.

First translate the general square-unit formula into AlphaNormalization for an arbitrary isomorphism between the two actual module pullback paths. The four coefficient comparisons and adjunctions of actualSquare p j R are definitionally the specified ones, and its site comparison is squareSiteIso because its commutativity proof is pullback.condition. This translation is proved while the isomorphism is a variable, preventing unnecessary kernel unfolding of the selected compositor. Apply the translation to exchangeModuleSquare and its general square-unit proof. The resulting statement is exactly AlphaNormalization for exchangeModuleSquare.symm. No nonemptiness or nonzero-ring assumption is used.

lean.statement:
theorem actual_open_square_alpha_normalization {P T U : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : P ⟶ T) (j : U ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1}) :
    ProEtaleOpenRestriction.AlphaNormalization p j R
      (actualSquare p j R).exchangeModuleSquare.symm
